## Establishment log (doubtful readings, misprints, other-print differences — the notes must say so)

# Establishment log — bardo-thodol-010 (pp. 90–98), 2026-11-22

Text **ga**, the second part: days eight to eleven of the wrathful bardo, which are Buddha, Vajra, Ratna and Padma Heruka. There is no
transcription of this print for ga. So three readers (all on the strongest model; no Sonnet role ran) read the images line by line from scratch,
with the other recension (readings/witness_ga.txt) open only as a guide to which words to expect:
- Reader A read 90.2 (rest)–92.
- Reader B read 93–95.
- Reader C read 96–98, and p. 99 only to see where the sentence ends.

Each reader also checked the line where their pages meet the next reader's. All three joins are clean. The full tables are in
readings/read_A-log.md, read_B-log.md and read_C-log.md.

## Layout
- Every page has five lines, 43 print lines in all, plus the rest of 90.2.
- pp. 91, 93, 95 and 97 are leaf fronts with the swirl ornament, written ༄༅༔ ༔ as in 009. 93.1 is a short line closed by an empty framed box.
- n98 and n99 are skewed (+2.8° and −1.8°), so C read them from straightened copies.
- **Start.** The part starts on 90.2 with འདི་དང, right after 009's …མི་སྲིད་དོ༔.
- **End.** The part ends at 98.3 …ཐིམ་ནས་སངས་རྒྱས་པར་འགྱུར་རོ༔, the close of the eleventh day (Padma Heruka). Nothing later on p. 98 closes a
  sentence. **Part 011 begins on 98.3 with ཡང་དེ་ལྟར་ངོ་སྤྲད་ཀྱང…** (the twelfth day).

## A gap set aside (README rule 7)
- **92.1, Buddha Heruka's last left-hand implement.** The print reads `ཐ་མ་ ⟨two stacks⟩ བསྣམས་པར༔`.
  - Reader A could not read the two stacks. The editor looked at ×10 and could not either. The first is a ཀ/ཁ-like letter with a subscript; the
    second has a ཊ-like head over a curled subscript.
  - A khaṭvāṅga (ཁཊྭཾ) is possible but not confirmed, and the other recension gives no candidate. Its item for this slot, ཐོང་གཤོལ, already
    stands in the print in the middle hand.
  - The two stacks are **left out of the established text**, which reads ཐ་མ་བསྣམས་པར༔. The draft must put a `gap` on that unit, and a gaps.json
    entry, saying an implement is missing here.
- **92.1, an uninked blank** of about 45 px after བར་བ་ན་ and before ཐོང་གཤོལ. The other recension has the skull-cup བྷན་དྷ in the middle hand
  here. A word was probably erased from the block or never cut. Nothing is printed, so nothing is written; the note should say so.

## Where the print differs in sense from the other recension (the print is followed)
- 90.5: the print adds དགོས་བྱུང་བ.
- 91.5: the sun and moon, snakes and dry skulls are all on the head; the fresh skulls on the body are missing.
- 92.1: the plough is in the middle left hand.
- 92.3: ཀླད་པའི་ཤར་ནས, "from the east of your brain", where the other recension has "from inside".
- 92.5–93.1: མ་འཇིགས་ཤིག where the other recension has མ་སྐྲག་ཅིག.
- 93.3→4: the print lacks "listen without distraction" for day nine.
- 94.3: the print lacks the "recognise him as your own awareness … yidam" passage, and has མོས་པ་གྱིས་ཤིག for མོས་གུས.
- 94.4: the print lacks ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་པའི་སྐུར.
- 95.2: the print lacks ཀྱི༔ བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས.
- 96.4: "flees back through the power of bad habits".
- 96.5: the deity host of the Padma family comes to meet him.
- 97.2: the centre face is "blazing" dark red, with a real ། after དཀར་བ.
- 97.5: དགའ་བ་བསྒོམ་ཤིག, "meditate on joy".
- 98.3–4: "there are those who do not meet it".
